facts.text: Blackjack was a backdoor pilot: USA Network and producers hoped star Dolph Lundgren's bodyguard Jack Devlin would become a weekly series. The show was never picked up.
John Woo wasn't just directing: he was also an executive producer on Blackjack, alongside Terence Chang, Christopher Godsick and screenwriter Peter Lance.
Director John Woo made this between Hollywood films, in a roughly three-year gap after Hard Target (1993). His next big one was Face/Off (1997).
Before Blackjack, John Woo made Face/Off (1997). He rejected its script several times until the studio rewrote it to suit him, dropping the futuristic setting. It grossed over $100 million in the US.
Saul Rubinek (Jack's roommate Thomas) played the pulp writer W.W. Beauchamp in Clint Eastwood's Unforgiven (1992) and later Donny Douglas, Daphne's fiancé, on Frasier.
Though released first, Blackjack was shot after Dolph Lundgren's The Minion and Sweepers, which he made back to back before it.
Blackjack was Kam Heskin's first screen role: John Woo cast her as supermodel Cinder James. Later in 1998 she joined the NBC soap Sunset Beach as Caitlin Deschanel.
Andrew Jackson plays rival bodyguard Don Tragle here. He also played Sgt. Andrew Scott's namesake... in Universal Soldier, the same Sgt. Andrew Scott role Lundgren played in that series.
Padraigin Murphy, who plays Casey, had a very short film career. According to a reviewer on the City on Fire site, it amounted to Blackjack plus a few Goosebumps appearances.
Jack Devlin's fear of white is leukophobia, a real term. Slashfilm notes how odd it is for a movie hero to be built around fear of a color. Lundgren wears sunglasses to cope.
Before Super Bowl I, Fred Williamson (Tim Hastings) predicted he'd flatten Packers receivers: 'Two hammers to Dowler, one to Dale should be enough.' He was knocked out in the fourth quarter.
After spinal surgery at age three, John Woo couldn't walk properly until he was eight. As a boy in a Protestant family, he wanted to become a Christian minister.
Lundgren holds a master's degree in chemical engineering and was offered a Fulbright scholarship to study at MIT before Rocky IV made him an action star.
Before the psychiatrist role here, Kate Vernon (Dr. Rachel Stein) played Lorraine Prescott on the CBS soap Falcon Crest in 1984-85 and appeared in Spike Lee's Malcolm X (1992).
Fred Williamson (Tim Hastings) played in Super Bowl I for the Kansas City Chiefs and earned the nickname 'The Hammer' for his hard hits.
Fred Williamson (Tim Hastings) played Dr. Oliver 'Spearchucker' Jones in Robert Altman's M*A*S*H (1970), then became a blaxploitation lead in Black Caesar (1973).
AllMovie's reviewer called this a weak John Woo film, but said it contains one carefully choreographed slow-motion shootout that bears his signature.
Phillip MacKenzie, who plays obsessed killer Rory Gaines, later turned up in Zack Snyder's Dawn of the Dead remake (2004) and in Hollywoodland (2006).
Kate Vernon (Dr. Rachel Stein) was Benny Hanson in Pretty in Pink (1986) and later played Ellen Tigh in the Battlestar Galactica reboot.
Kam Heskin (Cinder James) later replaced Julia Stiles as Paige Morgan in The Prince & Me 2: The Royal Wedding (2006), then returned for the direct-to-video third and fourth films.
Goof hunters spotted a typo in Jack Devlin's computer research on Cinder's wedding: the web page header reads 'Annoucements' instead of 'Announcements'.
TV Guide gave Blackjack 2 of 4 stars: 'Though it boasts several rousing action sequences, the film is sabotaged by lackluster acting, thin characterization, and a derivative storyline.'
Reviews on the City on Fire site split wildly: 'James H.' called Blackjack 'the lowest point in John Woo's career', while 'American Ninja' gave it 7.5/10 and said it 'delivers the goods'.
Reported to have aired again on USA Network on September 15, 1998, the film drew a 2.7 national rating.
Kate Vernon (Dr. Rachel Stein) is the daughter of actor John Vernon. Her sister is singer Nan Vernon.
Blackjack was shot in Toronto, Ontario, and made by Alliance Communications and others for USA Network. Its TMDB-listed budget is $8 million.
Blackjack was shot on 35mm film with Panavision anamorphic cameras by cinematographer Bill Wong, so it was filmed like a feature even though it aired on USA Network.
Kam Heskin (Cinder James) is, per IMDb, a descendant of John Hancock, signer of the Declaration of Independence, through her maternal grandmother.
Dolph Lundgren was nearly rejected for Rocky IV as too tall. During filming, a punch he landed on Sylvester Stallone reportedly put Stallone in intensive care for nine days.
John Woo's usual dove imagery is a trademark of his films, symbolizing a character's soul being saved. Watch for his signature slow-motion gunplay instead in this TV outing.
Saul Rubinek (Thomas) won a Genie Award for Best Supporting Actor for Ticket to Heaven (1981), and later won the Alan J. Pakula Award for The Contender (2001).
Blackjack is name-checked in Kevin Smith's Jersey Girl (2004), and a different film called Blackjack (2018) also references it.
Grantland's Q&A with Dolph Lundgren called Blackjack 'John Woo's amazing failed TV pilot' about a Marshal-turned-bodyguard with a color phobia, whose climax is in a milk factory.
Sharp-eyed viewers spotted Dolph Lundgren's hearing-protection earplugs visible during the climactic gunfight.
Reviewer 'Mairosu' on the City on Fire site gave Blackjack 1.5 out of 10 and called it 'a proper pile of junk', though he praised Lundgren's neutral accent.
